content.intro: Learn machine learning and ai integration through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Machine Learning and AI Integration matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines machine learning and ai integration as part of advanced ecosystem and specialized applications. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Calling external model services; Background processing for expensive inference; Input validation and privacy; Timeouts and cost controls; Separating model computation from request handling. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Calling external model services
items.text: Calling external model services crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Background processing for expensive inference
items.text: Background processing for expensive inference crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Input validation and privacy
items.text: Collect only the data the application needs, restrict access, document retention and deletion, and ensure exports/logs/backups do not silently keep data longer than intended.

items.title: Timeouts and cost controls
items.text: For Timeouts and cost controls, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Separating model computation from request handling
items.text: Separating model computation from request handling affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
